Synopsis:
The player encounter Nightsong, an angelic Aasimar and daughter of Selune who has been trapped in the Shadowfell for a century, first to serve as fodder for Dark Justiciars to kill (they must kill a Selunite to ascend), and then to provide Ketheric with immortality through a soul cage. The player can meet her either alone or with Balthazar. Nightsong is defiant and full of rage. She is immortal, so her current trials are, for her, an annoyance, an indignity, but she knows she will ultimately have her revenge. She regards the player with haughty defiance until she is convinced the player is on her side. If she's freed, she'll have 2 big cinematics of becoming free and cleansed by Selune.

Off‑screen the party has reached her prison/vault (the Spear of Night and Ketheric’s designs are present), and Nightsong’s opening taunts presume the player is a Sharran or Ketheric agent—an accusation that fits if the player just killed or rejected Shadowheart. Repeated deaths have left her furious, contemptuous, and eager for vengeance, but she will reluctantly soften if convinced you truly mean to free her. If freed, the scene escalates into two large cinematics: she kneels, the player may lay a hand on her shoulder to release her, and Selûne’s cleansing follows.

- COL_KethericShowdown_KethericIntro.json: The scene opens with the player confronting Ketheric Thorm in the Colony boss chamber at the start of the fight; Ketheric believes Myrkul restored his daughter and intends to use the Prism to fulfill his destiny as the god’s Chosen. Off‑screen the player has already delivered the Prism and may have freed Nightsong from her soul cage (or left her dead), while Isobel can be absent, tadpoled, or already killed in prior actions; Jaheira may or may not be present. Earlier Tower/Barracks beats — mind‑melds by Absolute guards, the Audience/Execution rooftop events, and assaults on Moonrise — have put Myrkulite forces on high alert and influence NPC attitudes here. Ketheric is openly hostile, prepared to kill and raise foes as servants of Myrkul, and his lines reflect cold, zealous devotion and possession of his daughter.
